title: Applying the Agile Onion and the mindset characteristics
blurb: Diagnose which Agile Onion layer a problem sits in, and choose the action that shows the right mindset characteristic.
question: Callowmere's web team runs every Scrum event but nobody can explain why it won't plan features beyond one sprint. Which onion layer has it adopted, and what is missing?

teach.body: Formally: the agile mindset is a way of thinking and approaching work that fosters adaptability and encourages continual learning, improvement and flexibility. The Agile Onion shows the layers of agile adoption: processes, practices, principles, values and mindset. In plain English: what a team does on the surface can look agile, but the deeper layers decide whether it really is. Your job in a scenario is to find the layer where the problem sits.

head: Layer
What it is
Exam hook
rows: Formal structure: when to deliver, how to manage work
Techniques and events, e.g. prioritization, workshops
Guidelines from the Manifesto, e.g. welcome late change
The way of thinking behind it all
teach.caption: Rows follow the syllabus list. The two facts examiners use most: practices are the most visible layer, and mindset is the core.

teach.h: Which layer is the scenario about?

children.edge: People and user value over process
children.label: Values (foundation)

children.edge: A way of thinking, learning, adapting
children.label: Mindset (core)

teach.body: The book describes key characteristics of the agile mindset, and the exam tests these five (do not rely on them being the full list): collaboration (shared ownership, co-creating with users and stakeholders); transparency and rich communication (information flows openly and is more than text, work status is visible, obstacles shared without fear); respect (empathy and open-mindedness, every voice valued); empowerment (autonomy and self-management); adaptability (inspect and adapt).

head: Characteristic
Stem cue
Missing when...
rows: Team designs alone, shows at the end
Every choice made above the team

teach.h: Answering 'which action BEST applies the mindset?'
items: Name the characteristic the stem is missing (who is excluded, what is hidden, who decides).
Prefer the option that includes the whole team, not selected people.
Prefer visible, shared, regular information over private or optional updates.
Reject options where the project manager speaks for the team or decides for it.
Reject options that add tools or events but leave the mindset untouched.

teach.body: At Callowmere University, wellbeing staff work across two campuses, some part-time or remotely, and adviser Tom Brierley openly doubts the hub. If a triage workshop lets two senior counsellors decide while others send comments later, respect is missing: invite every voice, including Tom's. If the web team's dashboard is kept where wellbeing staff cannot see it, transparency is missing: make the status visible to all.

teach.text: Classic traps: practices, not processes, are the most visible layer; do not key 'processes are the outer layer'. Values are the foundation that encompasses all else; principles explain the why. Respect is empathy and open-mindedness; freedom to decide is empowerment. Adding more practices does not fix a mindset problem.

items: Onion layers (syllabus list): processes, practices, principles, values, mindset.
Practices: most visible, only the surface. Values: the foundation. Principles: the why. Mindset: the core.
Characteristics: collaboration, transparency and rich communication, respect, empowerment, adaptability.
Best action: include everyone, make work visible, let the team decide, adapt from feedback.

summary: You can now place a scenario's problem in the right layer of the Agile Onion, from visible practices down to the mindset. You can also name the mindset characteristic a behaviour shows or lacks and pick the action that restores it.

A.q: Callowmere University's web team runs sprint planning, daily stand-ups, reviews and retrospectives, and keeps a story board. When the pro vice-chancellor asks why the team will not commit to features more than one sprint ahead, nobody in the team can explain the reason. Which layer of the Agile Onion has the team adopted without the deeper layers?
A.why: Practices (techniques and events) are the most visible aspects of agile adoption but only scratch the surface; teams that stop there may look agile without the deeper understanding (2.6.1).

whyNot.0: Principles are what explain the why, which the team cannot do.
whyNot.1: Values are the foundation; nothing in the stem shows the team living by them.
whyNot.3: Mindset is the innermost layer, the way of thinking the team appears to lack.

A.q: During a Callowmere workshop to redesign triage, the two most senior counsellors decide the new process. Other wellbeing staff, including adviser Tom Brierley who doubts the hub, are asked to email comments afterwards. Which action would BEST apply the agile mindset characteristic of respect?
options: Let the senior counsellors decide, as they know students' needs best
Hear every participant in the workshop, including doubters, before deciding
Ask Tom to stay out of the workshops until he supports the new hub
Ask the project manager to decide the triage design to avoid any conflict
A.why: Respect is rooted in empathy and open-mindedness, so all voices are valued and diverse perspectives are embraced (2.6.2).

whyNot.0: Experience matters, but leaving others to comment afterwards does not value every voice.
whyNot.2: Excluding a doubter is the opposite of open-mindedness and valuing all voices.
whyNot.3: Having the project manager decide removes the team's voice and its self-management.

A.q: Callowmere's web team is given authority to decide how it builds the booking features and how it splits its own work, within the release goals agreed with the project manager. Which characteristic of the agile mindset does this BEST show?
A.why: Empowerment fosters autonomy and self-management within teams; freedom to make decisions is its signal (2.6.2).

whyNot.0: Respect is about empathy, open-mindedness and valuing all voices.
whyNot.1: Adaptability is about inspecting and adapting in response to change.
whyNot.2: Collaboration is about shared ownership and co-creating with others.

B.q: At a Callowmere sprint review, the student design panel asks to change the booking flow it approved two sprints earlier. Rebecca Lyle tells them: 'Changing your mind now helps us build the right thing; late changes are welcome.' Which layer of the Agile Onion does her attitude reflect?
B.why: Principles are the core guidelines derived from the Agile Manifesto, such as welcoming changing requirements even late in development (2.6.1).

whyNot.0: Practices are techniques and events; the stem is about a guiding belief.
whyNot.2: Processes give formal structure for when and how work is done.
whyNot.3: Values are the Manifesto's core values; welcoming late change is one of its principles.

B.q: Callowmere's web team keeps its team dashboard in a folder that only the team can open. Wellbeing staff hear about delays to the booking feature through rumours. Which action would BEST apply transparency and rich communication?
options: Have the project manager email a monthly progress summary to managers
Keep the dashboard private but answer staff questions when they ask
Make the dashboard visible to wellbeing staff and walk them through it
Send wellbeing staff a written status report every Friday afternoon
B.why: Transparency and rich communication means information flows openly and is more than text, with clear visibility of current work status (2.6.2).

whyNot.0: A monthly summary from the project manager is infrequent, filtered and text-only.
whyNot.1: Answering on request keeps the work status hidden.
whyNot.3: A written report is text-only and is pushed rather than openly visible.

B.q: At each sprint review, Callowmere's web team looks at how students actually used the booking tool that fortnight and changes its plan for the next sprint as a result. Which characteristic of the agile mindset does this BEST show?
B.why: Adaptability is about inspection and adaptation in response to change (2.6.2).

whyNot.1: Empowerment is about autonomy and freedom to decide; the stem stresses inspecting and changing course.
whyNot.2: Respect is about empathy and valuing all voices.
whyNot.3: Transparency is about open, visible information; the stem is about acting on what was learned.

C.q: Callowmere's web team already runs every Scrum event well. To make the university 'become agile', the change office proposes adding a Kanban board and planning poker to the team's routine. Is this an appropriate way to build the agile mindset, and why?
options: Yes, because practices guide what agile teams do day to day
Yes, because processes give structure to agile implementations
No, because practices are the visible layer and do not build the mindset
No, because Kanban techniques cannot be combined with Scrum events
C.why: Practices are the most visible aspects of agile adoption but only scratch the surface; teams focusing on them may appear agile without the mindset (2.6.1).

whyNot.0: Practices do guide what teams do, but adding more of them does not reach the deeper layers.
whyNot.1: Processes do give structure, but alone they do not guarantee agility.
whyNot.3: Teams can combine techniques from different approaches; this is not the reason.

C.q: Callowmere's web team designs the self-referral form on its own and first shows it to the students' union at the Release 1 sign-off, even though the union offered a student design panel. Is this an appropriate application of the agile mindset, and why?
options: Yes, because the team is empowered to decide how it designs its work
Yes, because the panel can test the form during acceptance at the end
No, because students' union approval is needed for every user story
No, because collaboration means co-creating the solution with users
C.why: Collaboration means working closely with team members, stakeholders and users, with shared ownership and co-creation of solutions (2.6.2).

whyNot.0: Empowerment covers how the team works, but it does not justify excluding users from design.
whyNot.1: Testing at the end is the late quality check that agile tries to avoid; it is not co-creation.
whyNot.2: Nothing requires the union to approve each story; the problem is the lack of collaboration.

C.q: Chloe Hartley sets up a short online check-in that remote and part-time wellbeing staff can join, and a shared board showing which triage changes are in progress. Is this an appropriate application of the agile mindset, and why?
options: Yes, because open information and visible work status build trust
Yes, because remote and part-time staff need closer supervision
No, because rich communication needs everyone in the same room
No, because team status should be shown on the project dashboard
C.why: Transparency and rich communication: information flows openly, regular meetings and clear visibility of work status build trust and alignment (2.6.2).

whyNot.1: The purpose is openness and alignment, not supervision.
whyNot.2: Rich communication is about more than text; it does not require one room.
whyNot.3: The project dashboard serves the board; teams keep their own visible status too.

reteach.title: Find the layer, name the trait
reteach.question: Can you locate a problem in the onion and pick the action that fixes it?

blocks.body: Layer: events and techniques with no 'why' are practices; a Manifesto principle in action is principles; people and user value over process is values; the way of thinking is mindset. Characteristic: who is excluded (respect), what is hidden (transparency), who decides (empowerment), who co-creates (collaboration), does feedback change the plan (adaptability)?

blocks.text: More practices do not fix a mindset gap. Freedom to decide is empowerment, not respect.

explain.body: The core values come from the Agile Manifesto. They are the foundation that encompasses all else and shift the focus from rigid processes to people, collaboration and user value.

test.q: Callowmere's wellbeing director says the hub team must put conversations with students and staff ahead of following its procedures to the letter, and judge success by value to students. Which layer of the Agile Onion is he describing?
test.why: Values, defined by the Agile Manifesto, are the foundation of agile and shift the focus from rigid processes to people, collaboration and user value (2.6.1).

whyNot.0: Practices are specific techniques and events.
whyNot.1: Processes are the formal structure, which he is placing below people.
whyNot.2: Principles are the guidelines that explain the why, such as welcoming late change.

explain.body: Practices are techniques (such as prioritization) and activities (such as events and workshops). They are the most visible part of adoption, but teams that stop there may look agile without the mindset.

test.q: Visitors to Callowmere's web team see stand-ups, a story wall and retrospectives, and conclude the team is fully agile. Which layer are the visitors seeing?
test.why: Practices are the most visible aspects of agile adoption and only scratch the surface (2.6.1).

whyNot.1: Mindset is the deepest layer and cannot be seen directly.
whyNot.2: Values are the foundation, not what visitors observe.
whyNot.3: Principles are the guidelines that explain why the events are held.

explain.body: Empowerment fosters autonomy and self-management within teams. Whenever a stem stresses freedom to make decisions, think empowerment.

test.q: Northmere's integration developers say they have no freedom to decide how they test the records link; every choice must be approved by their account manager first. Which characteristic of the agile mindset is lacking?
test.why: Empowerment fosters autonomy and self-management; lacking freedom to decide is its absence (2.6.2).

whyNot.0: Respect concerns empathy and valuing all voices.
whyNot.2: Collaboration concerns shared ownership and co-creation with others.
whyNot.3: Adaptability concerns inspecting and adapting to change.

explain.body: Respect is rooted in empathy and open-mindedness: every voice is valued and diverse perspectives are embraced. When some people are left out or talked over, respect is the missing characteristic.

test.q: In Callowmere's retrospectives, the two developers who joined most recently are rarely asked for their views, and their ideas are dismissed quickly. Which characteristic of the agile mindset is MOST lacking?
test.why: Respect, rooted in empathy and open-mindedness, ensures all voices are valued (2.6.2).

whyNot.0: Adaptability is about inspecting and adapting; the stem is about who is heard.
whyNot.1: Empowerment is the team's freedom to decide, not how members treat each other's views.
whyNot.3: Transparency is about open, visible information rather than valuing each person's voice.
